title: feat: rank listed apps in app_top_weekly and trim catalog descriptions
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Split out of #14472 (website v2). Its home page "Live apps" and the /apps page show the top 8 apps from `app_top_weekly`.

- **`app_top_weekly`:** credits each App Key to the owner's catalog listing whose URL covers its redirect URI. Without a URL match, it credits the owner's listing when the owner has exactly one. Before, the ranking returned the key's own redirect URL, so unreviewed apps could appear. Counts only final, billed, successful production requests. Adds `limit` (default 10). Output columns are unchanged.
- **`app.json`:** shortens 132 descriptions that were cut off mid-word at 200 characters or were marketing copy.
- **Docs:** updates the `app_top_weekly` row in `public-stats.md`.

Prod, last 7 days (read-only SQL), paid BYOP requests from listed owners:

| Rule | Covered |
|---|---|
| URL match only | 1,018 of 18,773 (5%) |
| URL match + only-listing fallback | ~99% |

New top 3: OpenCode Pollinations Plugin (8,619), URV AI Chat (7,571), Pollinations AI Studio (1,411). Trade-off: an owner with one listing gets all their app traffic credited to it, including unlisted side apps (97 requests in this sample).

Follow-up: #15924 (link App Keys in `app.json`).

- Tinybird `deployment create --check` on staging: valid, only `app_top_weekly` modified, no data copied
- `app.js validate`: 856 apps OK
- After merge: deploy the pipe to staging, then prod

gist.headline: A tidier app garden
gist.blurb: The app charts get better at finding the actual app behind an App Key. And 132 catalog descriptions get to finish their sentences.
gist.summary: The `app_top_weekly` ranking credits successful, final, billed production requests to owners’ catalog listings instead of App Key redirect URLs, adds a `limit` parameter defaulting to 10, and trims 132 app descriptions.
gist.impact: The home page’s top eight Live apps and the /apps page will draw from ranked catalog listings, with shorter descriptions that do not end mid-word.
